title: The power of AI tools for prototypes
author: daddywookie
selftext:
https://preview.redd.it/b6wxxl0uypth1.png?width=1822&format=png&auto=webp&s=e76e7c917f371425ad1790a4162fea8e9eb06c4f

One of the most impressive and useful tasks I am enjoying with AI game development is the ability to quickly prototype ideas.

I am working on a mountain tycoon game and after days working on road building I got bored and decided to spend a Monday night generating terrain. I asked Codex to start exploring what was possible and after a couple of hours I now have a full Alpine mountain lab.

It pulls in topo data, allows me to select a slice to render and gives me control over the scaling, fine detail, season, lighting and trees. If I think of something I want to explore it takes a couple of minutes and then off I go again.

I know we get lots of one shot game prototypes being thrown around but, if you are working at a slower pace like me and exploring what you want your game to be, the speed with which you can experiment is so exciting.

Anyway, just wanted to share as I thought this was a good example of how I am using AI at the moment and how we can move beyond AI slop into thoughtfully crafted games.
